display.purpose: The name in the hero, in its lettering box. One per page.

headline.purpose: Section titles and inner-page band titles; smaller lettering steps name pillars, Work entries and About sections.

body.purpose: All running text, oldstyle numerals, max 68ch.

label.purpose: Navigation, scoreboard keys, roles, stack lines, dates, footer links. Never a lead-in above a heading.

motion.name: ease-paint

motion.name: paint-in

motion.name: flap
motion.purpose: Scoreboard values rotate over on load (staggered 140ms per cell) and again on hover and focus.

motion.name: reduced-motion

narrative.overview:
The site is a tennis venue seen from above. A matte blue court sits inside a green surround; white painted lines divide it with real court proportions (78 by 36 ft: singles alleys at 12.5%, service lines at 23.1% from each baseline). The content lives where things live at a club: the name is painted on the court, the four pillars are kept on a black club scoreboard with amber values, work is posted on a results board, and anything meant for reading is set on a white scoresheet. The athlete mindset is the structure, not a decoration on top of it.

Everything is flat paint. There is no radius, no shadow and no gradient, because a painted court has none; depth is the order of materials (surround, court, line, board, sheet), never light. Density is calm: long vertical rhythm between sections, generous panel padding, measured serif text. Painted lettering (Archivo at its widest, heavy caps) carries names and section titles; Source Serif 4 carries Greg's own voice.

It refuses the dark-slate developer portfolio: gradient names, particle fields, tool-chip grids and card grids.
keyCharacteristics: Flat painted materials in a fixed set: court blue, surround green, line white, board black, ball amber.
White lines are solid bars of fixed width (4px lines, 6px frames and nets) that stop at painted lettering boxes.
Wide heavy caps for anything painted; a serif for anything spoken or read.
Square corners everywhere, including photographs and code blocks.
Motion is a club's motion: lines paint in once, scoreboard values flap over.

rules.name: The Five Materials Rule
rules.body: Every surface is surround, court, line, board, or sheet. A new surface picks one of these; no tints, washes, or blends between them.

rules.name: The Amber Is A Score Rule
rules.body: Ball amber marks a value, a link, or focus. It is never a background block bigger than the skip link, and never body copy.

rules.name: The Mist Belongs To Its Ground Rule
rules.body: Each mist is paired with its ground: court-mist on court, board-mist on board, surround-mist on surround. Never move a mist to another ground.

rules.name: The Paint Or Voice Rule
rules.body: Expanded heavy caps for anything painted on a surface (names, section titles, scores); the serif for anything spoken or read. Do not set paragraphs in Archivo or titles in the serif.

rules.name: The Tabular Score Rule
rules.body: Years, dates and scoreboard values switch to tabular lining numerals; everywhere else, numerals stay oldstyle.

rules.name: The Flat Paint Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, no drop-shadow, no gradient, no backdrop blur, on any element in any state.

rules.name: The Lettering Box Rule
rules.body: Type placed over court lines sits on its own court-blue patch with a few pixels of padding, and the lines stop at its edge. Never let a line cross lettering, and never lift type off the court with a shadow.

dos: Do build every surface from the five materials: surround, court, line, board, sheet.
Do draw court geometry with solid white bars (4px lines, 6px frames and nets) at real court proportions.
Do put type that crosses court lines on a court-blue lettering box so the lines stop at its edge.
Do set names, section titles and scores in Archivo 800 at wdth 125, uppercase, line-height 0.9; set everything read or spoken in Source Serif 4.
Do use ball amber only for scores, years, links on dark grounds, focus and selection.
Do present lists as ruled tables with a fixed year or date column, not as cards.
Do keep motion to paint-in and flap, and make it static under reduced motion.
donts: Don't round any corner, including images and code blocks (0px everywhere).
Don't use box-shadows, gradients, glows or blur; depth is material order.
Don't reintroduce the dark-slate developer portfolio: gradient names, particle backgrounds, tool-chip grids, card grids.
Don't put a small uppercase label above a heading as a lead-in; labels name a value or an action.
Don't set small text in surround-mist or amber on the green surround; both fall below 4.5:1 there.
Don't move a mist color off its own ground.
